text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- President Suleyman Demirel unexpectedly includes the parliament speaker and chairman of the constitutional court in consultations on formation of new government.
- Experts in state's planning department say they plan to peg U.S. dollar at 200,000 Turkish lira, with inflation at 75 to 80 percent.
MILLIYET
- Radical Islamist deputy Halil Ibrahim Celik resigns from Welfare Party.
- Central bank says current account deficit is $713 million, including the unregistered suitcase trading -- up dangerously by 400 percent from last year.
HURRIYET
- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal says he will support a three-way coalition, including the Islamists, if a date for early elections is set before any vote of confidence.
- The finance minister announces civil servants will be paid inflation-indexed salaries.
YENI YUZYIL
- Demirel will consider all government alternatives, including main opposition's proposed broad-based "reconciliation" formula.
- Islamist culture minister empties Ayasofya museum in northern Trabzon province and turns the Bodrum castle chapel into a mosque.
RADIKAL
- Schools begin 86-days summer holiday on Friday.
CUMHURIYET
- Radio and television watchdog suspends broadcasts of private Islamist television channel for one day after a debate programme insulted the armed forces.
DUNYA
- Unregulated capital grows rapidly in Turkey.
ZAMAN
- Conservative coalition leader Tansu Ciller says any government formulea excluding the Islamist Welfare Party will not ease tensions in the country.
